price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: PNR failure (defense suppresses the primary ball-screen action)
PULL_UP as a counter after a failed PNR
league-wide consistency across units (share of units with lift>0, median lift)
lift in percentage points against a baseline
methodological_questions: Is 'lift>0 in >=70% of units and median lift >2pp' a valid and adequately powered criterion given per-unit noise?
How can PNR failure be defined from play-by-play without using the outcome?
What is the lift relative to: the pull-up share, pull-up efficiency, or total possession PPP after failure?
How should units, the baseline and selection into a pull-up after a failed PNR be handled (shot clock, regression to the mean, player quality)?
Does the effect replicate across seasons and between regular season and playoffs, and how are multiple counters handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Attempt to label on-ball coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup and play-by-play fields reached only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) confident labels. switches_on was not populated. Recorded verdict: failed_gate. Limits recorded: small sample and label error.

The A1 adapter PPP lift did not behave like a real coverage response. no_signal teams (+0.1260) did better than adapters (+0.0667). Adapter minus no-signal was negative at 1 and 2 votes. The next-game carryover test was null (Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842). Limits recorded: label error and selection/regression to the mean.

Teams that shifted toward 'counter' play types gained about +0.05 to +0.06 PPP later in the game, but the SWITCH subgroup reversed. The no-signal baseline had the highest dPPP. Limit recorded: selection/regression to the mean.

Descriptive star-suppression cells. Giannis's forced PULL_UP gave PPP 0.848, 0.540 below his preferred DRIVE. The record notes no placebo or matching, and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Regular season to playoffs: PULL_UP PPP allowed +0.341 with possession share -7.6pp; PNR share +12.1pp. No inferential test. The PNR share jump may reflect tagging differences. Based on 25 teams.
Star suppression profiles after a preceding opponent play type. Rank-1 deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control.
Descriptive shot-level PNR rates by team (e.g. OKC 7.6% to IND 13.8% of half-court shots). PBP-derived PNR is a proxy, and possession-level rates are higher.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling defensive coverage from NBA matchup and play-by-play fields
failed_approaches.why: Very low confident-label rates (14.9% and 3.3%) and an unpopulated switches_on field. Recorded limits: label error and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a PPP lift for 'adapting' teams as evidence of a real counter response
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact from labelling and selection/regression to the mean. The wrong-way and no-signal comparisons did not behave as a real response would, and there was no carryover.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game 'did_adapt toward SHOULD counters' as evidence that counters work
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact. The limit is selection/regression to the mean. The no-signal baseline was highest, and the SWITCH subgroup reversed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading forced-play-type PPP gaps as suppression effects
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching. The record notes later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

evidence_establishes: No returned record tests PULL_UP lift after a failed PNR, per unit or league-wide.

Prior attempts to infer defensive scheme or counter response from this play-by-play data have repeatedly failed or been recorded as artifacts. The causes were labelling error, selection/regression to the mean and small samples.
Derived play-type tagging, including PNR, is noisy and may differ between regular season and playoffs (FAM:SF-APPS-012). PNR is also a proxy built from play-by-play (FAM:SF-APPM-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP has positive lift after PNR failure in any unit.
Whether a defensible outcome-independent definition of PNR failure exists in this data.
Whether per-unit sample sizes can support a 70%-of-units criterion.
Any causal effect of pull-ups as a counter, since the records are descriptive or artifact-flagged.
own_inferences: 'Fail' is probably defined by outcome (no shot, a miss, or a turnover). That would make the label outcome-derived and mechanically bias any conditional lift. A process-based definition is needed, such as no screener-roll or drive shot or foul within N seconds, with the ball handler still holding the ball.
'Lift' is not defined. It could be pull-up share, pull-up eFG, or possession PPP. The 2pp threshold suggests share or eFG, but this must be fixed before any analysis.

Conditioning on a failed PNR puts the possession late in the shot clock. Pull-ups after a failed PNR are likely forced shots by good shot creators, which gives shot-clock and shooter-selection confounding and possibly a mechanical floor or ceiling.

The 70%-of-units rule is noise-dominated. If the true lift is 2pp and per-team SE is about 5pp, only about 65% of teams would show lift>0 by chance alone. A true uniform effect could therefore fail the rule, and a null effect could still show about 50% positive. The test needs shrinkage or a permutation null on the positive fraction rather than a raw count.
A positive result is more likely to be an artifact of selection than a real counter, given the history of artifact verdicts in adjacent adaptation work.
uncertainties: The number of failed-PNR possessions with a pull-up per team-season is unknown. It is probably about 50-150, so power is likely low.
The data description lists 2025-26 playoffs as complete from 2026-06-21, after the question date of 2026-05-23, so playoff data were partial when posed.
Whether the possession-level PNR tags are accurate enough, and stable across seasons, is unknown. The tag may even be a pull-up by construction.
The unit (team, player or defender) and the baseline are unspecified.
I did not read the full record text for the cut-off families (SF-APPA-001 and SF13).

historical_effect.explanation: The question looks like a routine counter-lift test. The prior records show that similar counter-lift results were artifacts (FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF13) and that scheme labels from this data were largely untestable (FAM:SF-APPS-058). They moved me from 'proceed' to 'proceed_with_changes'. The changes are a process-based, outcome-independent PNR-failure label, a shot-clock-matched baseline, a placebo, and a probabilistic replacement for the raw 70% rule.

blocking_constraints.text: 'PNR fail' must be defined without using the possession outcome. If it is defined by outcome, the lift is mechanical.
Per-unit counts of pull-up-after-fail shots are probably too small for a 70%-of-units rule to be reliable at a 2pp effect.
PNR is a proxy from play-by-play, and prior scheme labelling failed at low coverage.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tests this question. Adjacent counter and adaptation studies were recorded as artifacts or untestable, and descriptive pull-up findings had no controls.

risks.text: A failure label built from the outcome makes conditional shot quality mechanically biased. Use pre-outcome process criteria.
Shot clock, shooter quality, defender and score state affect both the choice of a pull-up and its efficiency. Control or match on them.
Units chosen for extreme PNR failure rates, or players chosen as pull-up specialists, will regress. Units should be defined from a prior period.
Noise makes the share of positive units about 50-65% even under a real small effect. Pre-compute power by simulation.
Proxy PNR and pull-up tagging errors. Validate on a hand-labelled sample and report the misclassification rate.
A late-clock pull-up is the default shot type, so pull-up share is inflated mechanically after failure.
Without placebo alternatives such as DRIVE, SPOT_UP or other pull-up contexts, a positive lift cannot be attributed to the failed PNR.
If other counters are tested alongside PULL_UP, adjust for it. Fix thresholds in advance.
Pull-up rates and tagging may drift across seasons and between regular season and playoffs.
Do not define units or baselines using data from the evaluation period.

design.estimand: For each unit, the difference in pull-up eFG% (pp) after a failed PNR versus a baseline of pull-ups in the same shot-clock band without a failed PNR, adjusted for shooter. A secondary estimand is pull-up share of the second action. Define 'fail' pre-outcome as a PNR-tagged possession where, within N seconds of the screen, there is no shot, free throw, roll-man pass or drive by the ball handler and the ball handler still holds the ball. Do not use miss, turnover or points.
design.unit: Primary unit: offensive team-season, with 30 teams in each of 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. Secondary unit: ball handler with at least a pre-set minimum of pull-ups after a failed PNR.
design.sample: Discovery: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons. Confirmation: the 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs are treated separately, and 2025-26 playoffs are excluded because they were partial on 2026-05-23. A unit is eligible only if it has at least the pre-set minimum of qualifying shots, fixed before looking at the lift.
design.power: Before analysis, simulate the share-positive rule under true lift 0, 2 and 4pp using the observed counts per unit and binomial noise. Report the probability of passing the rule under each. Expect low power at about 50-150 shots per unit. If the rule's pass probability at 2pp is under about 0.8, replace the raw 70% rule with the hierarchical estimate (below).
design.controls: Shot-clock band, period, score margin, shooter (random effect), defending team, home/away and season. Hand-validate the PNR, failure and pull-up labels on a random sample and report the error rate. Estimate team lift by partial pooling to limit regression to the mean. Define units from a prior period.
design.falsification: Placebo contexts: pull-ups after non-PNR possessions at matched shot-clock times, and a fake 'fail' defined by a random timestamp. Compare with DRIVE, SPOT_UP and other counters after the same failure. Check that the share-positive result is not reproduced by label shuffling within a team (permutation null). Require the same sign in discovery and confirmation seasons. Run a label-quality sensitivity analysis at stricter and looser failure windows N.
design.multiplicity: A single pre-registered primary test (PULL_UP, primary estimand, team-season unit). Any other counters or alternative definitions are secondary and adjusted by Holm or FDR.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if, in both discovery and the confirmation season, (a) the permutation-calibrated share of units with lift>0 is >=70% and exceeds the permutation null, (b) the median pooled lift is >2pp with a 95% interval excluding 0, (c) placebo contexts show no comparable lift, and (d) the label-validation error rate is within the pre-set bound. If (a) is unattainable under the power simulation, report 'untestable at this unit size' rather than rejecting. Rejected if powered and the pooled interval excludes 2pp. Otherwise report inconclusive.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API play-by-play files and the derived play-type possession graph for 2022-23 through 2024-25 (regular season and playoffs) and 2025-26 regular season as of 2026-04-13. Freeze the file hashes and the tagging code version before analysis. The 2025-26 playoffs are excluded as partial on 2026-05-23.

research_concepts: pull-up jump shot as counter to defensive suppression
lift in efficiency (percentage points) over baseline
methodological_questions: Is lift>0 in at least 70% of units with median lift above 2pp a valid criterion for a real league-wide counter?
How should PNR failure be defined without outcome-derived labels?
How to define baseline and units, and handle small samples per unit and regression to the mean?
How to guard against confounding by player skill, shot selection and defense type, and multiple testing across counters?
Is the pull-up lift robust across seasons and regular season vs playoffs?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
